walkthrough: Liquid pressure acts perpendicular to the surface, so forces on the top and bottom are vertical and forces on the sides are horizontal, all pointing into the block.
For equal area $A$, force is $F = pA$, so arrow length is proportional to pressure $p = h\rho g$ where $h$ is depth below the surface.
The bottom face is deeper than the top face, so the upward arrows on the bottom must be longer than the downward arrows on the top.
On the vertical sides, depth $h$ increases from top to bottom, so horizontal arrows must get progressively longer downward.
At any given horizontal level the depth is the same on left and right, so left and right arrows at the same height must be equal in length.
Only diagram A shows short downward top forces, longer upward bottom forces, and left-right symmetric side forces that increase with depth. This is option A.
